catalog_quote: Stress occurs on the first syllable regardless of weight, and on every syllable which surfaces with a long vowel (Rice 1992, 63-65). When morphological concatenation results in adjacent strings of syllables all of which have long vowels, the even numbered syllables in that string surface with a short vowel and no stress.. (Rice 1992:65) ... [passage 1004:] Systematic exceptions with stress on the second syllable exist, especially in di-syllabic stems ... sources.note: Sole primary description of Gidabal stress; our coding (weight/CVV, initial default, second-syllable shift, alternate long-vowel shortening) is a database paraphrase of Rice's summary of this book. Reading its phonology/stress pages would convert grade 'carried-quote' to a primary quote and settle whether every non-initial long vowel is stressed (Rice) or weight matters only in the first two syllables (Goedemans 1998 cat. VI 'QS marginal').
